paper_metadata.title: MWO2KG and Echidna: Constructing and exploring knowledge graphs from maintenance data
paper_metadata.venue: Proceedings of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers, Part O: Journal of Risk and Reliability
paper_metadata.abstract: Unstructured technical texts contain engineering knowledge that is underused for data analysis. Maintenance work orders capture information about what work was done on an asset and why, but their short text fields are unstructured, terse and jargon-rich. The paper addresses efficient extraction of technical information from work-order text and its combination with structured fields such as dates, functional locations, and asset make and model. It presents a technical-language-processing solution: Echidna is an interface for querying and visualising historic asset data as a knowledge graph, while MWO2KG uses deep learning and annotated training data to construct the graph from unstructured technical text combined with structured fields. The tools are tested on maintenance work-order and delay-accounting data from industry partners and support reliability-engineering activities including failure-modes-and-effects analysis, maintenance-strategy validation, and process improvement. Source code for both tools is reported as available on GitHub under the Apache 2.0 License.

code_and_data_availability-28-03.section: Echidna – an interactive knowledge graph visualisation and query interface
code_and_data_availability-28-03.excerpt: The demonstration graph has been constructed from a set of publicly available maintenance work orders.

problem_addressed: The paper addresses the difficulty of extracting useful engineering knowledge from terse, jargon-rich maintenance work-order text and combining it with structured asset records so that reliability engineers can query historical maintenance information, identify failure modes, validate maintenance strategies, and support process improvement.

methodology.description: MWO2KG converts technical short maintenance text and associated structured fields into a Neo4j knowledge graph. Deployment begins with annotation or import of work orders in Redcoat using maintenance-specific entity types such as item, activity, observation, and location. The annotations are preprocessed to retain at most one entity label per token. A Flair NER model uses pretrained character-level embeddings, a bidirectional LSTM, and a softmax classifier trained with stochastic gradient descent to label entities. A separate Flair text-classification model maps extracted observations to failure-mode codes. Postprocessing adds asset-hierarchy labels using ISO 15926 rules and normalises misspellings and inconsistent names using a manually curated correction dictionary. Triple generation links each item to every other entity in the same short work order through heuristically assigned relations; functional locations are linked to entities in the corresponding work order, and optional downtime events are linked to functional locations with cost and duration properties. The resulting triples are imported into Neo4j. Echidna then visualises and queries the graph, supporting node filtering, aggregation, functional-location filtering, structured-field queries, and failure-mode grouping using ISO 14224 categories. The paper explicitly notes that a relation-extraction step is shown in the generalised architecture but is not implemented in MWO2KG.

ontology_or_schema_use.value: The annotation schema contains 10 maintenance-specific entity types, including item, activity, observation, consumable, location, agent, attribute, cardinality, specifier, and time. ISO 15926 supplies the asset hierarchy used to add parent asset-class labels during postprocessing. ISO 14224 supplies failure-mode categories, condensed to 19 codes for the failure-mode classifier in the described system; the evaluation dataset is also described as originating from 22 ISO 14224 codes. Echidna supports aggregation of classes and subclasses in these hierarchies.

input_output.input_type: Short, unstructured technical maintenance work-order text combined with structured work-order fields, functional locations, and optionally downtime-event data.
input_output.input_granularity: Work-order short-text fields and individual observations/entities within work orders; structured records are associated at work-order, functional-location, and downtime-event levels.
input_output.output_representation: A Neo4j knowledge graph containing entities and relationships/triples, including maintenance items, activities, observations, locations, functional locations, and optional downtime-event nodes with properties such as cost and duration; Echidna provides a visual and queryable representation.

models_and_tools: Echidna web-based graph visualisation and query interface
Pretrained Flair mix-forward and mix-backward character-level embeddings
Bidirectional LSTM and softmax token classifier
Neo4j graph database and Cypher query language
datasets: NER dataset: 4,002 manually annotated maintenance work orders, split into 3,200 training, 401 validation, and 401 test work orders; 10 entity types; annotations produced by 10 University of Western Australia research-group annotators.

Failure-mode classification dataset: 626 observation/label pairs, split into 502 training, 62 validation, and 62 test pairs; labels derived from ISO 14224 failure-mode codes, with minority-class upsampling in training.
Industry-partner maintenance work-order and delay-accounting data; the paper does not provide partner names or a full public dataset description.
A publicly available maintenance-work-order set is used for the Echidna demonstration graph.

metrics: Per-class precision, recall, and F1-score for NER
Per-class precision, recall, and F1-score for failure-mode classification
Micro-F1 and Macro-F1 for failure-mode classification
Qualitative inspection of example predictions and confidence values
baselines: No quantitative baseline for the complete MWO2KG pipeline, because the authors state that suitable baseline datasets are unavailable.
Contextual comparison with reported state-of-the-art NER F1 scores of approximately 0.90–0.94 from other clean news-report settings; this is not a matched experimental baseline.
evaluation.setting: Two component-level supervised experiments use held-out test splits. NER is trained on 3,200 work orders, validated on 401, and tested on 401. Failure-mode classification is trained on 502 observation/label pairs, validated on 62, and tested on 62; minority classes are upsampled in training. The full graph-construction pipeline and triple-generation quality are not quantitatively evaluated. Tables 2–5 report component metrics and representative predictions.

value: NER achieved Micro-F1 0.828 and Macro-F1 0.858 on the held-out test set.
NER per-class F1 ranged from 0.640 for Attribute to 1.000 for Specifier; Item achieved 0.795, Observation 0.803, Activity 0.904, and Location 0.847.
Failure-mode classification achieved Micro-F1 0.597 and Macro-F1 0.459 on its held-out test set.

Failure-mode classification performed well for Overheating (F1 1.000), Minor in-service problems (0.733), Plugged/choked (0.667), Leaking (0.667), and Structural deficiency (0.600), but poorly for several ambiguous or minority classes, including Breakdown (0.375), Low output (0.000), Failure to stop on demand (0.000), High output (0.000), Erratic output (0.000), and Spurious stop (0.000).

Qualitative examples show that character-level modelling handled spelling errors, missing spaces, abbreviations, and noisy technical text, although some predictions disagreed with noisy or ambiguous ground-truth labels.
The authors present the combined tools as a way for reliability engineers to visualise historic asset data, identify failure modes, and query by functional location or asset class.

Combines unstructured text with structured work-order, functional-location, and optional downtime data.

Provides an end-to-end operational workflow from annotation and extraction to graph construction and user-facing visualisation/querying.
Uses explicit maintenance taxonomies, ISO 15926 asset hierarchy rules, ISO 14224 failure modes, and a correction dictionary to improve semantic grouping and graph usability.
Makes the source code for MWO2KG and Echidna available under the Apache 2.0 License.
